newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's Savimbi invited to S. African summit.
newsitem.headline: Angola's Savimbi invited to S. African summit.

text.p: Southern African leaders want Angola's veteran guerrilla leader Jonas Savimbi to return to the capital Luanda for the first time in four years for a summit to discuss Angola's fragile peace process.

A Zambian delegation formally invited Savimbi during a meeting with him on Saturday in his UNITA-controlled central highlands town of Andulo, said Zambia's former foreign minister Vernon Mwaanga, who headed the delegation.

South Africa's President Nelson Mandela, Zimbabwe's Robert Mugabe and Zambia's Frederick Chiluba have already said they will attend the summit of the 12-state Southern African Development Community (SADC) in Luanda next Wednesday.

Mwaanga told Reuters on his arrival back in the government-controlled capital that he had also expressed the Zambian president's concern about lack of progress in implementing the 1994 peace protocol.
Mwaanga said he could not give a definite answer on whether or not Savimbi would attend the meeting.
Zambia hosted peace talks between the Angolan government and UNITA in 1994 to end two decades of civil war that erupted soon after independence from Portugal in 1975.
Both sides signed the Lusaka agreement in November of that year and are currently in the process of completing the implementation of its timetable.
Diplomats have said the peace process has reached the final stage but that key aspects of the accord have yet to be fully implemented.

Savimbi, who has disarmed almost all of his 62,500 fighters over the past year, has been reluctant to return to Luanda for security reasons, despite guarantees for his safety by Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos.
